subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should this issue be resolved with latency-specific Slack HTTP Request URL guidance, or should OpenClaw change Slack setup/default behavior beyond the existing `mode: "http"` support?
rationale: HTTP mode already exists, but deciding whether to document the latency trade-off, change setup prompts, or change defaults affects Slack operator deployment expectations.

options.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
options.body: Keep Socket Mode as default for local/private deployments and update Slack docs/setup guidance to prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

options.title: Change setup or defaults
options.body: Have maintainers sponsor a stronger setup/default change that steers new hosted Slack installs toward HTTP mode with upgrade and operator guidance.

options.title: Accept current guidance
options.body: Decide the existing deployment-shape transport table is sufficient and close after recording that no extra latency-specific guidance is planned.

recommendation.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
recommendation.body: Keep Socket Mode as default for local/private deployments and update Slack docs/setup guidance to prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the measurements, authored the related channel-side fixes, and explicitly scoped the remaining HTTP-guidance decision.
